key_insight: High-pressure torsion transforms TiZrHfNbTa into a nanostructured, defect-rich alloy where electrons dominate heat transport and phonon scattering controls the smaller, strain-dependent thermal response.
engineering_relevance: Severe plastic deformation can be used to tune refractory high-entropy alloys for applications needing controlled thermal/electrical transport alongside high hardness and strength.
method: HPT severe plastic deformation of equiatomic TiZrHfNbTa
Nanostructure/defect engineering via dislocation accumulation, grain refinement (~40 nm), and partial BCC-to-omega transformation
Thermal and electrical transport analyzed with Wiedemann-Franz separation of electron vs phonon contributions
evidence_signal: The abstract reports hardness reaching a steady state, specific heat showing non-monotonic strain dependence, thermal conductivity decreasing then slightly recovering, and electrical conductivity decreasing monotonically after HPT.
watch_item: The phonon/electron partition relies on model-based interpretation (Wiedemann-Franz), so deviations from ideal assumptions or microstructural inhomogeneity could affect the quantitative split.
paper_title: Thermal and electrical conductivity of a refractory high-entropy alloy after high-pressure torsion: Electron versus phonon contributions
